Subject: Vanguard Consulting — Activation brief & technical enablement plan

Alex —

Thanks again for the productive conversation earlier. Attached is a concise activation brief tailored for Vanguard Consulting that outlines the recommended enablement path for the integration partner track, roles & responsibilities, and a proposed 4-week technical ramp. Highlights:

- Week 0: Admin & security review (KMS, logging, network)
- Week 1: Test environment setup & sample connector deployment
- Week 2: Shared evals & performance tuning
- Week 3: Production cutover plan + rollback runbook

Can you confirm the two technical contacts you want on the deep-dive? We'd like to schedule a 90-minute technical design session the week of Apr 17 to walk through VPC peering, model variant choices (hosted vs dedicated), and cert rotation.

I've attached: vanguard_activation_brief_v1.pdf for your review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Confirm date/time for the deep-dive
2) Share any existing network diagrams or security questionnaires
3) We'll prepare a draft SOW to review during the session

Thanks,

Alex —

Appreciate the quick reply. Apr 18 10:00 PT works for us; we've tentatively blocked calendar time. A few technical clarifications ahead of the deep-dive so we can prep a short runbook:

1) AWS account model: is this a separate account per environment (dev/test/prod) or a single-account multi-VPC setup?
2) KMS: will Vanguard manage keys (CMKs) or should we plan to integrate Redwood-managed encryption? We typically recommend customer-managed CMKs for compliance-sensitive integrations.
3) Egress & firewall: do you currently allow outbound TLS to redwood-inference.com on 443? If not, please provide the firewall change window.
4) IP allowlist vs DNS: are you able to accept our short-lived egress IP ranges, or do you prefer DNS-based allowlist for service routing?

Attached is a simple topology diagram and a sample security checklist we use during partner onboarding.

For the pilot, given BYO-VPC preference, we'll propose a minimal IAM role and an isolated subnet pattern in the draft SOW. We'll also include optional Dedicated pooling notes if you decide to evaluate that in parallel.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
